body:
Round 3, reviewed at `aac6056d` (delta `dcc7104a..aac6056d`, 4 commits, +459/-235). Verification harness and evidence: <https://github.com/cheyang/rbg/tree/verify/pr416-api-compat-toggle/docs/verification/pr416-api-compat-toggle>.

**Requesting changes on two things**, both left inline: the upgrade guard (`upgrade-guard.yaml`) and the dropped-rule guard in `hack/gen-helm-rbac`.

## What this delta got right

`clusterrole.yaml` and `manager.yaml` now read the toggle with the *identical* expression, so the granted RBAC and the rendered `--enable-deprecated-workload-types` flag can no longer disagree — that closes the string-`"false"` and empty-value footguns properly, not just symptomatically. `gen-helm-rbac` gained strict decoding, a `kind: ClusterRole` assertion and 223 lines of tests, and its output is deterministic. The chart README no longer contradicts itself on what the toggle rejects, and the PR description now matches the shipped design. I re-ran the earlier regression guards: the default is consistent and the toggle is effective, there is no chart/RBAC drift (209 == 209), generated artefacts are in sync after `make manifests generate`, and a real API server accepts all 12 rendered objects in both value shapes.

`cacheOptions` listing StatefulSet and Deployment unconditionally is also the right call, and the comment's reasoning is correct — `ByObject` is per-type configuration, not an allowlist, and creates no informer.

## On the design reversal

`ValidateUpdate` is back to the whole-object check, so last round's grandfathering is gone and the round-1 denials (F2a/F2c/F9/F10) are reachable again. **I am not re-filing those as regressions.** The PR body, both READMEs, `values.yaml`, `NOTES.txt` and the flag help now say the same thing — `false` is fresh-install-only — and under that premise such objects cannot exist. It is a coherent choice, and making create and update run the identical check closes last round's asymmetry (the parent's update being exempt while the child RBG it must *create* was not) by construction rather than with a second special case.

But the whole design now rests on that single premise, which is why the first inline comment is the blocking one: nothing enforces it. Close that, and the reversal becomes safe and those findings close as a class.

## Correction to my own previous review

**I was wrong to file F8/F8b as blockers, and I'm withdrawing that.** That `false` makes v1alpha1 unusable unless every role names `RoleInstanceSet` explicitly is now documented in six places as intended behaviour. It is a deliberate cost, not a defect, and it should not block this PR.

Also: last round I said the upgrade guard could only be discussed in the summary because `upgrade-guard.yaml` was unchanged by this PR. That was incorrect — the file is *added* by this PR, so it gets a proper inline comment this time.

## Still open, but not anchorable to the diff

- **Legacy reconcilers are still built when the deprecated types are off**, so nothing at the reconcile layer stops a read or write of a type whose RBAC the chart removed. Unreachable today only because admission refuses those objects — i.e. it depends on the same unenforced premise as above.
- **The `LWS_*` → `RBG_LWP_*` environment rename has no alias shim.** A container reading `LWS_LEADER_ADDRESS`, `LWS_GROUP_SIZE` or `LWS_WORKER_INDEX` after moving to `RoleInstanceSet` still starts and then fails at runtime: no admission error, no reconcile error, nothing on the RBG status. `DeprecatedEnvLws*` constants are declared but referenced nowhere.
- **`Chart.yaml` is still `version: 0.8.0-alpha.2`**, below the `0.8.0-alpha.3` line this guard is meant to draw. Worth rebasing regardless of which guard design you pick.

comments.body:
**`major`** — this guard carries two problems with the same root cause: it checks *whether the operation is an upgrade* rather than *whether the cluster is in a state this chart version can serve*.

**1. It breaks the command the repo documents.** `{{- if .Release.IsUpgrade }}` refuses every `helm upgrade`, so `helm upgrade --install` works exactly once per cluster. There are 10 call sites: `README.md:77`, `README-zh_CN.md:77`, `doc/install.md:30,66`, `doc/dev/how_to_develop.md:301`, `Makefile:249`, `test/stress/scripts/deploy-controller.sh:52`, and CI — `.github/workflows/e2e-test.yml:158`, `release-test.yml:117`. CI stays green only because `kind create cluster` gives each run a fresh cluster. `deploy/helm/rbgs/README.md` also contradicts itself: lines 63 and 154 forbid `helm upgrade`, line 70 prescribes `helm upgrade --install`.

**2. It does not enforce the invariant this PR relies on.** The PR argues `enabled=false` is coherent because "the sole supported way to reach `false` is a fresh install, where no such object can exist", and names this guard as the enforcement. It cannot see that path:

- the chart declares no CRDs (`crds/` is empty, no template emits one — they come from the `crd-upgrade` Job), so `helm uninstall` leaves every `RoleBasedGroup`/`RoleBasedGroupSet` in place;
- the reinstall has `IsUpgrade=false`, so the guard never runs;
- nothing inspects the cluster — no template uses `lookup`, and the `enabled=false` render succeeds unconditionally.

So `helm uninstall` → `helm install --set controller.deprecatedWorkloadTypes.enabled=false` — the procedure this very message prescribes — produces exactly the state the PR says cannot exist. Such an object is then unwritable on every path: the discovery-mode annotation patch (`rolebasedgroup_controller.go:363`), `kubectl scale`, the RBGSet template sync (`rolebasedgroupset_controller.go:465`), the HPA/scale-adapter update (`rolebasedgroupscalingadapter_controller.go:511`) and the child RBG create (`rolebasedgroupset_controller.go:231`) — with nothing written to the object's status.

**Suggestion:** gate on cluster state instead of `IsUpgrade`, carried by a `pre-install,pre-upgrade` hook Job — refuse when `enabled=false` and deprecated-workload objects already exist, and refuse upgrades when v1alpha1-era objects remain. One mechanism covers both problems, and `helm upgrade --install` becomes idempotent again so none of the 10 call sites need changing. Two details: `hook-weight` must be below `crd-upgrade.yaml`'s `-4` (otherwise the CRDs are already rewritten when the check runs), and reusing the controller's own `isDeprecatedWorkloadType` constants avoids a third hand-maintained copy of "which types are deprecated".

I measured the alternatives before suggesting this, rather than guessing:

- A chart-version marker + `semverCompare` works mechanically (I tested all six scenarios) but **cannot deliver the stated goal**: the marker would ship with this PR, while `0.8.0-alpha.3` is already released without it, so an upgrade from alpha.3 always lands in the "cannot determine" branch.
- A *template-level* check is the wrong carrier: `lookup` returns empty on `helm template`, `--is-upgrade` and client-side `--dry-run`, so a fail-closed template check false-fails `helm diff upgrade`. Hooks are not executed by `helm diff` at all, so a Job cannot false-fail it.

**`major`** — this guard cannot fire.

`splitRules` is not count-preserving: a rule whose resources straddle the gate emits **two** blocks, one kept and one gated (lines 186-192). A split inflates the count and pays for a drop.

Against the `config/rbac/role.yaml` committed in this PR: **16 rules → 18 blocks**, because the `apps` rule (`controllerrevisions` + `deployments` + `statefulsets`) and its `/status` counterpart both straddle. So the guard tolerates **two silently dropped rules today** — adding a single `urls=` kubebuilder marker would strip that permission from the chart ClusterRole with exit 0, no error, and no CI diff. That is the failure mode the guard was added to catch.

`TestSplitRulesDropsResourcelessRule` asserts `assert.Empty(t, blocks)` with no error, which pins the drop as *acceptable* at the `splitRules` level — so the behaviour is currently tested at the wrong layer.

**Suggestion:** reject any input rule that produced no output block, instead of comparing totals. I verified this makes the drop detectable in both the synthetic case and against the real `role.yaml` (it also requires updating `TestSplitRulesDropsResourcelessRule`).
